summary: Root cause identified with high confidence (0.86–0.87): the shared redis-cache lost its dataset at ~13:20–13:22Z when node redis-cache-2 failed its health check and an empty, still-resyncing replica was promoted, producing a cold cache (hit_ratio_pct 96%→13.75%, memory_pct ~70%→7.25%). market-data-service then fell into a cache-miss storm and rebuilt each quote from the exchange feed snapshot (1034–8748ms), blowing pricing-engine's per-quote deadline and stepping its p99 from ~60ms to ~1.4–2.3s. This matches HIST-107 ("Cold cache storm after redis failover") service-for-service and symptom-for-symptom. Alternative origins — exchange-gateway/feed degradation, auth-service v7.2.0 cookie hardening, and pricing-engine client-pool saturation — are each directly falsified by flat exchange-leg measurements, timing/topology, and unchanged local resources respectively.

ranked_hypotheses.title: redis-cache primary failure promoted an empty replica (cold cache) — HIST-107 repeat
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared redis-cache behind market-data-service and pricing-engine lost its dataset at ~13:20–13:22Z: node redis-cache-2 failed its health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts) and was marked primary-down at 13:22:10Z; the replica promoted at 13:22:52Z was EMPTY because it was still resyncing. That emptied the dataset, dropping hit_ratio_pct from ~96% to 13.75% and memory_pct from ~70% to 7.25%. market-data-service, whose quote lookups depend on the cache, fell into a cache-miss storm and had to rebuild each quote from the exchange feed snapshot (1.0–8.7s), which blew pricing-engine's per-quote deadline ('market-data-service took up to 8456ms'). The visible symptom is pricing-engine p99 stepping from ~60ms to ~1.4–2.3s and slow quotes on the trading screens; api-gateway inherits the same slow-but-successful path with no new 5xx. The exchange-gateway leg is measured clean, so the slow rebuilds are explained by cache loss plus the cost of refilling, not by a slow upstream feed.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache-2 primary fails health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts) at 13:22:10Z and a replica that was mid-resync is promoted to primary at 13:22:52Z, so the new primary's dataset is empty

Dataset is actually gone, not just reported: hit_ratio_pct collapses from ~96% baseline to 13.75% (cliff starting in the 13:21Z bucket, mid-bucket ~13:20–13:21Z) and memory_pct drops from ~70% to 7.25% — an emptied, near-zero dataset
This is not eviction/capacity pressure: evictions_per_min stays flat at ~2–5 keys/min and connected_clients stays at baseline ~304–314, so nothing was squeezed out and no client surge preceded it

market-data-service quote lookups now miss and it rebuilds every quote from the exchange feed snapshot: 289 WARN 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot' with rebuild times 1034–8748ms, from 13:22:25Z

market-data-service's own p99 steps abruptly from ~40ms baseline to 664.95ms avg / 1979.98ms max in the 13:18Z bucket, peaks at 1908ms avg at 13:24Z, and remains ~22x baseline (1014ms avg at 14:50Z) — the degradation is on this service's path, and it persists as long as the cache stays cold

The exchange-feed leg is NOT the slow leg: exchange-gateway's own latency_p99_ms is flat (mean 130.72ms, min 119.96, max 143.91) across the whole window with no step at onset, and its outbound upstream_latency_ms to the external exchange is likewise flat/constant (mean 119.92ms, min 111.19, max 130.39) — direct measurement of that leg shows no spike

Slow market-data-service responses exceed pricing-engine's per-quote deadline: 192/195 matched error records are 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <N>ms' (up to 8456ms), first at 13:23:57Z — numerically downstream of both the redis cliff and the first cache-miss warning
pricing-engine latency_p99 steps abruptly (not gradually) from a flat 54–66ms baseline to 1370.73ms avg / 2281.51ms max in the 13:20Z bucket, causing the reported 2–3s quote loads
api-gateway shows the same latency-only step (206.4ms → 1418.15ms avg / 2554.24ms max) with 5xx flat at ~0.2%, i.e. propagation of a slow-but-successful path rather than any gateway fault

No recorded deployment or config change exists on any quote-path component near onset — redis-cache, market-data-service and exchange-gateway all return 0 deployments and 0 config changes for 10:00–14:59Z, and pricing-engine had 0 — so the origin is an unrecorded runtime/infra event, exactly the HIST-107 pattern (redis failover with no change record)

the promoted replica's emptiness (F34) — rather than a separate simultaneous key-expiry/maxmemory event — is what emptied the dataset; F33's near-zero memory and F30's flat evictions are consistent with this but no raw keyspace counter exists to prove it

market-data-service's rebuild number (1034–8748ms) is dominated by refill work against a now-cold cache and not by a concurrent exchange-side stall (argued by F27/F28, which measure that leg as flat, but market-data-service's own span breakdown does not exist)

ranked_hypotheses.title: exchange-gateway / external exchange feed degradation slowed quote rebuilds
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The origin is the market side of market-data-service: exchange-gateway or the external exchange feed degraded around 13:20Z, so rebuilding a quote from the exchange feed snapshot took 1–8.7s. The 'cache miss storm' wording would then be a symptom of a slow refill path being exercised, and pricing-engine times out on market-data-service for that reason rather than because redis lost data.

causal_chain.claim: exchange-gateway or the upstream exchange feed degrades ~13:20Z (latency or partial unavailability)
market-data-service rebuilds from the exchange feed snapshot take 1034–8748ms and it logs 289 cache-miss-storm warnings from 13:22:25Z
Slow market-data-service responses (p99 stepping ~40ms → ~665–1908ms) cause pricing-engine deadline-exceeded errors ('market-data-service took <N>ms', up to 8456ms) from 13:23:57Z
pricing-engine p99 steps abruptly to ~1.4–2.3s and api-gateway inherits latency with no new 5xx
Absence of any recorded change on the quote path is consistent with an external-provider degradation

assumptions: a quote rebuild requires a live, slow exchange-gateway call
market-data-service's rebuild latency could be dominated by upstream exchange work rather than by cache-refill work
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Directly falsified by new measurement. exchange-gateway's own latency_p99_ms is flat (mean 130.72ms, min 119.96, max 143.91) across the entire window with no step at onset (F27), and its outbound upstream_latency_ms to the external exchange — the direct measurement of this very leg — is likewise flat and constant (mean 119.92ms, min 111.19, max 130.39) with normal onset-bucket values (F28). Meanwhile the redis leg demonstrably did fail: an explicit primary-failure log, empty-replica promotion, hit-ratio collapse to 13.75% and memory collapse to 7.25% (F34, F32, F33). exchange-gateway also shows 0 deployments and 0 config changes, closing the F18 coverage gap (F21, F22).

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service v7.2.0 SameSite=strict cookie hardening caused session re-auth churn
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only change in the fleet window, auth-service v7.2.0 'Session cookie hardening' (SameSite=strict) at 11:30Z, broke cookie replay on some client/proxy hop, forcing re-authentication and adding latency to the trading-screen request path.

causal_chain.claim: auth-service v7.2.0 sets SameSite=strict on session cookies at 11:30Z
Clients on some hop can no longer replay the session cookie, forcing re-auth or extra auth round-trips
Added auth round-trips inflate end-to-end request latency, showing as slow quotes
pricing-engine p99 steps and api-gateway degrades latency-only with no new 5xx

assumptions: auth-service sits on the quote-serving request path despite not being an edge for pricing-engine
cookie semantics can add seconds of per-quote latency
the ~1h50m quiet gap is explained by gradual cookie expiry
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing and mechanism both fail, and new evidence makes the real origin concrete elsewhere. The change landed 11:30Z with pricing p99 flat at 54–66ms through the 13:15Z bucket (~1h50m quiet gap) before an abrupt 13:20Z step (F7, F16, F25). auth-service is not an edge in pricing-engine's dependency graph (F6). The actual error signatures name market-data-service and redis-cache (F8, F9), and the earliest signal is redis-cache's own logged primary failure/empty-replica promotion and hit-ratio cliff (F34, F32), not any auth symptom. auth-service does share redis-cache (F23), but no auth-side symptom or auth log is implicated.

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine-side client/thread-pool saturation on the market-data-service HTTP call
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The origin is pricing-engine's outbound HTTP client to market-data-service: a connection/thread-pool limit saturated so calls queued and timed out with 'market-data-service took <N>ms' despite healthy local CPU/memory.

causal_chain.claim: pricing-engine's outbound HTTP client pool to market-data-service saturates and requests queue
Queued calls exceed the per-quote deadline, logging 'market-data-service took <N>ms'
p99 steps abruptly to ~1.4s and api-gateway inherits the latency with no new 5xx

assumptions: connection/thread-pool metrics would be saturated if queried
pool saturation could arise with zero deployments or config changes on pricing-engine
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Onset ordering and mechanism contradict it. A client-pool queue on pricing-engine cannot produce redis-cache's explicit primary-failure log, empty-replica promotion, hit-ratio collapse (96%→13.75%) or memory collapse (~70%→7.25%) — all of which are observed at redis-cache, the far end of the path (F34, F32, F33). market-data-service's own p99 steps to ~665–1908ms with the cache-miss storm at 13:22:25Z, before pricing-engine's first error at 13:23:57Z (F9, F25, F12). pricing-engine shows no local saturation (CPU 38–41%, memory 47–50%, unchanged at 13:20Z) (F10) and had no deployment or config change (F2, F13).

facts.statement: The quote-serving chain is pricing-engine → market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache); market-data-service → exchange-gateway (http) and redis-cache, and redis-cache is the only shared datastore on that path.

recommended_actions.action: Warm the promoted redis-cache primary now: preload/repopulate the quote key-space (or force a controlled backfill of recently-active quote keys) so hit_ratio_pct returns toward the ~96% baseline instead of the current ~36%.
recommended_actions.rationale: The dataset is genuinely empty (hit_ratio_pct 96%→13.75%→~36.6%, memory_pct ~70%→7.25%→23.06%) and market-data-service is still rebuilding ~22x slower than baseline; warming is the mitigation that resolved the identical HIST-107 incident.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back or hot-patch auth-service v7.2.0 and do NOT treat this as a client-side pool issue — hold the fleet as-is and focus remediation on redis-cache/market-data-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: The auth change predates onset by ~1h50m and auth-service is not an edge on the quote path, while the exchange leg and pricing-engine local resources are measured clean; a rollback would risk unrelated auth impact with no plausible mechanism.

recommended_actions.action: Verify redis-cache replica sync health before/while promoting in future failovers: fix the sync-check that allowed redis-cache-3 to be promoted while still resyncing (empty dataset), i.e. implement HIST-107's 'fixed replica sync checks' control.
recommended_actions.rationale: The explicit log line shows the promoted replica's dataset was empty because it was still resyncing, so the failover path itself produced the cold cache that caused the outage.

recommended_actions.action: Add and alert on a redis-cache hit-ratio / memory-floor guardrail (e.g. page when hit_ratio_pct drops abruptly or memory_pct falls below a floor) and add preload-on-promotion to the failover runbook.
recommended_actions.rationale: redis-cache exposes only connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct — no latency metric — so hit_ratio_pct and memory_pct are the only early-warning signals; both collapsed ~10 minutes before pricing-engine's first error.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm recovery by checking hit_ratio_pct back toward ~96%, memory_pct toward ~70%, and market-data-service p99 back to ~40ms after warming; keep the incident open until then.
recommended_actions.rationale: Recovery was only partial at 14:59Z (market-data-service p99 ~893ms, hit ratio ~36.6%), so the incident cannot be closed on symptom subsidence alone.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument quote lookups end-to-end: add a redis-cache latency/keyspace metric and a per-dependency span breakdown on market-data-service (cache-fill vs exchange-call) so future cold-cache events are directly measurable.
recommended_actions.rationale: redis-cache has no latency_p99_ms or keyspace counters, and market-data-service exposes no span breakdown, so attribution of its 665–1980ms p99 increase to the refill leg is currently indirect.

recommended_actions.action: Review the blast radius and hardening of the shared redis-cache: auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service all consume it, so size the cache and set maxmemory/eviction policy and capacity headroom for full-dataset loss on any single node.
recommended_actions.rationale: redis-cache is the only shared datastore in the graph, so its failure degrades multiple services simultaneously — this incident widened beyond the HIST-107 pair.

data_gaps: redis-cache exposes no latency_p99_ms metric and no keyspace_hits/keyspace_misses, evicted_keys, expired_keys or used_memory/maxmemory counters (only connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct), so the dataset loss and the lookup leg cannot be quantified in absolute keys or ms — evidence is hit-ratio/memory based plus one log line.
redis-cache cpu_pct was never retrieved (budget_exhausted), so redis-side CPU/IO saturation as a contributor to the PING timeouts cannot be fully excluded.

No redis-cache restart/failover event records were queryable in this session, so 'no earlier failover' is unverified; only the 13:22:10–13:22:52Z failover is visible in the retrieved 12:30–14:30Z log set and a contains='failover' re-query was not executed.

market-data-service has no per-dependency span breakdown (available metrics only cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), so its rebuild cost cannot be decomposed into redis-refill work vs any concurrent upstream work.
The market-data-service log result was truncated (30 of 291 matched), so the exact first cache-miss warning time could be earlier than 13:22:25Z.
Bucket resolution (5–6 min, and 2-min for the redis hit-ratio cliff) prevents pinning down sub-minute ordering between market-data-service's 13:18Z step and the redis 13:19–13:21Z hit-ratio cliff.

Change history proves absence only of recorded deployment/config objects; an unrecorded redis-side topology or maxmemory event would leave no row, so empty change history is not positive evidence against an unrecorded redis event.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that redis-cache never actually lost its dataset — e.g. a keyspace/uptime series showing the same keys present across 13:20Z, or a correction to the 13:22:52Z 'dataset on new primary is empty' log line — which would remove the mechanism H1 depends on.

A direct measurement showing the exchange-gateway outbound leg or the external exchange feed spiking at onset (upstream_latency_ms or exchange-gateway p99 stepping above ~130ms around 13:18–13:22Z), which would revive H2 as the origin of the slow rebuilds.

Detection of a recorded config/deployment change on redis-cache or market-data-service near 13:20Z (maxmemory, sentinel, timeout, autoscaling) in a data source not covered here, which would repoint the cause from failover to a configuration change.

Evidence that market-data-service's rebuild latency is dominated by upstream exchange work rather than cache refill (e.g. spans showing near-identical duration with a warm cache), which would break the causal chain from cold cache to pricing-engine timeouts.

Demonstration that pricing-engine's timeouts persist at baseline downstream latency (i.e. market-data-service p99 back at ~40ms while pricing-engine p99 stays ~1.4–2.3s), which would revive H4 (local client/pool saturation) as a co-cause.

findings.statement: Precedent for the current signature is infrastructure/dependency-driven, NOT a deployment: HIST-113 (pricing-engine CPU saturation) was capacity, HIST-102/HIST-103 were DB failover and external exchange outage; the only rollout-triggered precedents were auth-service HIST-101 (bcrypt cost, rolled back v6.4.0) and HIST-115 order-service pool misconfiguration ('Reverted config; added validation') -- both are deployment/config changes of the kind NOT present in this window.

No prior incident in the searchable set was resolved by rolling back a change we still suspect today: HIST-101 rolled back an auth-service release (v6.4.0, 2025-08-14) for login latency, but today's auth-service change is v7.2.0 (SameSite=strict cookie hardening), made 11:30Z -- and the 13:20Z onset is ~1h50m later, with no config/timeout/pool change recorded anywhere (T2, tc-010).

findings.statement: Topological fit: the degraded chain (market-data-service -> redis-cache, with pricing-engine calling market-data-service over http) exactly mirrors HIST-107's affected pair [redis-cache, market-data-service], and redis-cache is the only shared datastore on pricing-engine's path -- so a redis-cache-side event (cold cache / failover / eviction) explains both the market-data rebuild times (1034-8748ms) and the downstream pricing deadline-exceeded errors without any deploy.

Change-history coverage is incomplete precisely where it matters: exchange-gateway and api-gateway deployment queries were never executed (budget exhausted), so the change list cannot be called exhaustive for those two services.

findings.statement: redis-cache has ZERO deployments and ZERO config changes in 2026-04-09T10:00Z–14:59Z: get_deployments returned count 0 and get_config_changes returned count 0 for scope redis-cache, both complete (partial:false, no warnings). No maxmemory, timeout, sentinel, autoscaling or rollback change is recorded for redis-cache.

market-data-service likewise has ZERO deployments and ZERO config changes in the same window (count 0 for both queries, complete results with no warnings) — no config/flag/topology change on the cache-consuming service near or before the 13:20–13:22Z onset.

exchange-gateway — the service previously unqueried (budget-exhausted gap) — also returned count 0 deployments and count 0 config changes in 2026-04-09T10:00Z–14:59Z, closing that coverage gap: the change list is now confirmed empty for all three named services.

No change event of any kind was found near 13:20Z for any of the three services: the three deployment queries and three config-change queries returned empty arrays rather than any event timestamped around onset, so there is no config_change origin to attach to H1 from change history.

redis-cache is confirmed as the hub of the quote chain and the only shared node: edges caller->callee include auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service all 'to':'redis-cache' kind 'cache', while every service node in the graph has "shared":false except redis-cache (type redis, owner platform, "shared":true). This widens the blast radius beyond the HIST-107 pair — auth-service and portfolio-service also consume the same cache.

Precedent search for redis failover/restart/maxmemory returns only HIST-107 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' (2025-12-09, services [redis-cache, market-data-service], symptoms ['cache miss storm','quote latency'], root_cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica', resolution 'Warmed cache; fixed replica sync checks') — i.e. an infra event with no change record, matching the empty change history above; note the search returned no incident caused by a redis config/maxmemory change.

findings.statement: RETRY SUCCEEDED (previously 503, attempts:2). market-data-service latency_p99_ms (unit ms) was flat at ~38–40ms across 12:30–13:15Z (e.g. 38.4 at 12:30Z, 40.2 at 12:36Z, 40.45 at 13:12Z, max 44.61 in-window), then stepped abruptly to 664.95ms avg / 1979.98ms max in the 13:18Z bucket, reached its peak 1908.21ms avg at 13:24Z, and decayed only slowly (1553.12 at 13:54Z, 1237.98 at 14:24Z). Onset is ~13:18Z, i.e. BEFORE the 13:22:25Z first cache-miss log and before pricing-engine's 13:20Z bucket.

market-data-service's outage is still unresolved and in fact worsening relative to the pre-incident baseline at the latest data point: at 14:50Z p99 was avg 1014.99ms, declining to avg 893.39ms / max 893.39ms at 14:59Z — ~22x the ~40ms baseline, with 0 missing points in both the 6-min and 3-min resolution queries.

EXCHANGE-GATEWAY LEG IS CLEAN. exchange-gateway's own latency_p99_ms was flat for the whole 12:30–14:30Z window: mean 130.72ms, min 119.96ms, max 143.91ms, and individual buckets barely move across the onset (130.44 at 13:12Z, 132.19 at 13:19Z, 130.95 at 13:26Z). It shows no step at ~13:20Z despite having the most granular 420s buckets.

exchange-gateway's upstream_latency_ms (its outbound call to the external exchange) was likewise flat and constant across the window: mean 119.92ms, min 111.19ms, max 130.39ms, with the onset buckets at normal values (119.55 at 13:19Z, 121.54 at 13:26Z). This is the direct measurement of the exchange-gateway outbound leg and it did NOT spike.

REDIS LEG SPIKE — redis-cache hit_ratio_pct had two distinct signals, not one: a precursor drop to avg 47.37% in the 13:19Z bucket (max still 96.34%, i.e. the bucket is split), then a collapse to avg 13.75% / max 14.79% at 13:26Z, versus a ~96% baseline in every bucket from 12:30Z to 13:12Z (96.14, 95.84, 95.97, 96.23, 95.92, 95.88, 96.05). The cache then recovers only gradually (19.18% at 13:40Z, 36.73% at 14:29Z) — still far below baseline.

The redis leg's degradation is a HIT-RATIO/cold-key event, not an eviction or capacity event: evictions_per_min stayed flat at ~2.6–3.4 keys/min (mean 3.06, min 1.96, max 4.87) with the onset bucket at 3.35 and 2.71, and redis-cache exposes no latency metric at all (latency_p99_ms is not_found; available_metrics are connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct), so no direct redis latency series can be obtained.

redis-cache exposes NO keyspace_hits/keyspace_misses, evicted_keys, expired_keys, used_memory/maxmemory metric names — its only available metrics are connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct. So the requested raw counters must be substituted by these substitutes; hit-rate is available only as hit_ratio_pct.

redis-cache hit_ratio_pct shows a sharp cliff at ~13:20Z: flat at 94.5–96.9% through the 13:19Z bucket, then 53.4% (max 96.34) at 13:21Z, collapsing to 11.59–13.94% from 13:23Z onward and only slowly recovering (36.58% by 14:30Z). This is the hit-rate cliff the task asked about, and it is a genuine cache-cold event, not a gradual decay.

redis-cache memory_pct collapsed in the same bucket as the hit-rate cliff: ~69–71% avg through 13:12Z, 49.06% at 13:18Z, then 7.25% at 13:24Z — a near-empty dataset (min 6.0% for the window) that slowly refills to 23.06% by 14:30Z. The dataset was emptied, not memory-exhausted.

redis-cache logs show an explicit primary failure and empty-replica promotion immediately before the hit-rate cliff: 13:22:10Z ERROR 'node redis-cache-2 failed health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts); marking primary as down', then 13:22:52Z WARN 'failover: promoting replica redis-cache-3 to primary; dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)', followed by 2x 'MASTER <-> REPLICA sync started (full resync) for redis-cache-2' (13:28:42Z, 13:35:26Z) and a 'client reconnect storm' peaking at '92851 new connections in 10s' (13:40:15Z). No such event exists earlier in the 12:30–14:30Z window.

findings.statement: redis-cache shows NO resource pressure or client surge as the cause: evictions_per_min stayed flat at 1.96–4.87 keys/min across the entire 12:30–14:30Z window (no eviction spike at 13:20Z), and connected_clients remained ~304–314 avg on every bucket except two artifact buckets with depressed averages (216.91 at 13:18Z, 219.34 at 13:24Z) whose maxima stayed normal (314.11, 312.87). After the failover, clients briefly reconnected 13:30–13:40Z but the average did not exceed the pre-incident ~310–314 baseline range (post-window max 340.95).

Onset ordering tightened with 2-minute buckets: the hit-ratio cliff begins in the 13:21Z bucket (avg 53.4, max still 96.34 — i.e. degradation starts mid-bucket ~13:20–13:21Z), which precedes market-data-service's first cache-miss warning at 13:22:25Z (F9) and pricing-engine's first deadline-exceeded error at 13:23:57Z (F8). The redis failover log lines (13:22:10Z primary marked down, 13:22:52Z empty-replica promotion) fall inside/just after that bucket. This places a redis-cache-side cold-cache event at or before the earliest downstream symptom, not after it.
